children.title: Why Calculus?
Why do we need limits to find areas?
children.summary: Fills a circle with polygons of 6, 12, 24 … sides; their areas creep up to πr² but never reach it in finitely many steps (Archimedes)

children.title: Why is a tangent the limit of secants?
children.summary: Slides the second point toward the first and watches the secant settle into the tangent

children.title: Why is 'speed right now' a limit?
children.summary: Shrinks the time interval for an average speed: 1 s, 0.1 s, 0.01 s … and the values settle

children.title: Why can infinitely many steps take finite time?
children.summary: Runs Zeno's Achilles and tortoise: the infinitely many catch-up times add to a finite total

children.title: Newton, Leibniz and the invention of calculus
children.summary: Reads a timeline of who found what, and why the two notations both survived

children.title: The Limit Idea
Why doesn't a limit care about the point itself?
children.summary: Fills, empties and moves the dot at x = a; the limit doesn't change

children.title: Why do left and right limits have to agree?
children.summary: Approaches a jump from each side and gets two different answers

children.title: Why does sin(1/x) have no limit at 0?
children.summary: Zooms toward 0 and finds infinitely many wiggles, all between −1 and 1

children.title: Why can a calculator lie about a limit?
children.summary: Evaluates (√(t² + 9) − 3)/t² for ever-smaller t; the true limit is 1/6, but rounding eventually shows 0

children.title: Why is '→ ∞' not a number?
children.summary: Watches 1/x² grow past every bound you set; an infinite limit describes how the function behaves

children.title: Estimate a limit from a table and a graph
children.summary: Zooms the graph and fills in the table together

children.title: Limit Laws
Why can you just substitute for polynomials?
children.summary: Sees there's no gap or jump to worry about; that's what continuity will mean

children.title: What does 0/0 tell you?
children.summary: Factors and cancels to reveal the hole, then reads the height of the hole

children.title: Why does the squeeze theorem work?
children.summary: Traps x² sin(1/x) between −x² and x²; both squeeze to 0

children.title: Why is lim (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = naⁿ⁻¹?
children.summary: Factors xⁿ − aⁿ = (x − a)(xⁿ⁻¹ + … + aⁿ⁻¹), then substitutes x = a

children.title: Limit-law stepper
children.summary: Applies the sum, product and quotient laws one at a time with a reason shown

children.title: Rationalise to find a limit
children.summary: Multiplies by the conjugate to clear a 0/0

children.title: The Precise Definition
What does 'as close as you like' really mean?
children.summary: Plays the ε–δ game: you pick a band ε around L, the tool finds a δ window that fits (spec below)
children.spec: Game: the student drags an ε band around L; the tool shades the largest δ window whose graph stays inside the band. Shrink: an ε slider down to 0.001 shows δ always exists for a limit that's true. Failure: a jump function where no δ works for small ε, so the student sees why the limit doesn't exist. Formula strip: |x − a| < δ ⇒ |f(x) − L| < ε, with live numbers.

children.title: Why does δ depend on ε, and on steepness?
children.summary: Steepens the function and watches the δ window shrink

children.title: Limits at infinity: the N version
children.summary: Sets a band around the asymptote and finds where the graph enters it for good

children.title: ε–δ proof builder
children.summary: Writes the proof for linear and quadratic examples with each choice explained

children.title: Continuity
Why does 'no lifting the pen' need three conditions?
children.summary: Breaks each condition in turn: the value is missing, the limit is missing, or they disagree

children.title: Three kinds of discontinuity
children.summary: Sorts removable, jump and infinite breaks

children.title: Why must a continuous path cross every level? (IVT)
children.summary: Walks a climber from 1000 m to 3000 m; they must pass 2000 m, unless the path jumps

children.title: Make a piecewise function continuous
children.summary: Picks the constant that joins the pieces

children.title: Two opposite points on the equator with equal temperature
children.summary: Applies the IVT to the temperature difference around a circle

children.title: Limits at Infinity
Why do dominant terms decide horizontal asymptotes?
children.summary: Divides by the highest power and sees the other terms fade (see Functions & Graphs → Rational Functions)

children.title: Why does eˣ beat every power, and ln x lose to every power?
children.summary: Races eˣ against x¹⁰⁰ and ln x against x^0.01 far out

children.title: Why is ∞ − ∞ undetermined?
children.summary: Finds that √(x² + x) − x → ½, while other ∞ − ∞ forms give 0 or ∞

children.title: Divide by the highest power
children.summary: Steps through rational and root examples
